claim: By directed evolution in the laboratory, populations of Escherichia coli were generated that exhibit extreme resistance to ionizing radiation.
source: By directed evolution in the laboratory, we previously generated populations of Escherichia coli that exhibit a complex new phenotype, extreme resistance to ionizing radiation (IR).
evidence: This claim is supported by the authors' previous experimental work described in the manuscript.

claim: The evolved E. coli isolates exhibit a 3-4 order of magnitude increase in IR resistance at 3000 Gy.
source: The molecular basis of this extremophile phenotype, involving strain isolates with a 3-4 order of magnitude increase in IR resistance at 3000 Gy, is now addressed.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental measurements of survival at 3000 Gy described in the manuscript.

claim: Of 69 mutations identified in one of the most highly adapted isolates, the IR resistance phenotype is almost entirely accounted for by only three nucleotide changes in the DNA metabolism genes recA, dnaB, and yfjK.
source: Of 69 mutations identified in one of our most highly adapted isolates, functional experiments demonstrate that the IR resistance phenotype is almost entirely accounted for by only three of these nucleotide changes, in the DNA metabolism genes recA, dnaB, and yfjK.
evidence: This claim is supported by functional experiments described in the manuscript showing that these three mutations account for most of the IR resistance phenotype.

claim: Four additional genetic changes make small but measurable contributions to IR resistance.
source: Four additional genetic changes make small but measurable contributions.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing small increases in IR resistance from additional mutations.

claim: Genetic innovations involving pre-existing DNA repair functions can play a predominant role in the acquisition of an IR resistance phenotype.
source: Genetic innovations involving pre-existing DNA repair functions can play a predominant role in the acquisition of an IR resistance phenotype.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental findings that mutations in DNA repair genes (recA, dnaB, yfjK) account for most of the IR resistance.

claim: Deinococcus radiodurans can absorb IR doses in excess of 5 kGy without lethality.
source: Deinococcus radiodurans, which can absorb IR doses in excess of 5 kGy without lethality (over 1000 times the lethal dose for humans), has become a key model organism for understanding this phenotype (Cox and Battista, 2005, Blasius et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: D. radiodurans can absorb IR doses over 1000 times the lethal dose for humans.
source: Deinococcus radiodurans, which can absorb IR doses in excess of 5 kGy without lethality (over 1000 times the lethal dose for humans), has become a key model organism for understanding this phenotype (Cox and Battista, 2005, Blasius et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature and established scientific knowledge.

claim: IR can lead to damage of protein, DNA, and all other cellular macromolecules mainly through the formation of reactive oxygen species (ROS).
source: Mainly through the formation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), IR can lead to the damage of protein, DNA, and all other cellular macromolecules (Sonntag Cv, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: A condensed nucleoid structure could potentially facilitate DNA repair processes.
source: These are (A) a condensed nucleoid structure, which could potentially facilitate DNA repair processes (Zimmerman and Battista, 2005, Levin-Zaidman et al., 2003)
evidence: This claim is presented as a potential mechanism supported by citations.

claim: An enhanced capacity for amelioration of protein damage could protect DNA repair systems and make them more readily available following irradiation.
source: (B) an enhanced capacity for amelioration of protein damage, which could protect DNA repair systems and make them more readily available following irradiation (Daly, 2012, Daly, 2009)
evidence: This claim is presented as a potential mechanism supported by citations.

claim: Potential specialized pathways for DNA repair may contribute to IR resistance.
source: (C) potential specialized pathways for DNA repair (Zahradka et al., 2006, Cox and Battista, 2005).
evidence: This claim is presented as a potential mechanism supported by citations.

claim: The amelioration of protein oxidation has received extensive experimental support as a mechanism to account for much if not all of the observed IR resistance in D. radiodurans.
source: The amelioration of protein oxidation has received extensive experimental support as a mechanism to account for much if not all of the observed IR resistance in D. radiodurans (Daly et al., 2004, Slade and Radman, 2011, Krisko and Radman, 2010, Daly, 2012, Daly, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: Increases in cytosolic antioxidant capacity, particularly an increase in the cellular Mn/Fe ratio, appear to make major contributions to IR resistance in D. radiodurans.
source: Increases in cytosolic antioxidant capacity, particularly an increase in the cellular Mn/Fe ratio (Daly et al., 2004), appear to make the major contributions.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Increasing the Mn/Fe ratio limits the Fenton chemistry that produces ROS.
source: Increasing the Mn/Fe ratio limits the Fenton chemistry that produces ROS (Krisko and Radman, 2010, Daly, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature and established biochemical knowledge.

claim: The hypothesis that the condensed nucleoid of Deinococcus facilitates efficient DNA repair has been questioned, since the presence of condensed nucleoids does not correlate reliably with radiation resistance in bacterial species.
source: The hypothesis that the condensed nucleoid of Deinococcus facilitates efficient DNA repair has been questioned, since the presence of condensed nucleoids does not correlate reliably with radiation resistance in bacterial species (Zimmerman and Battista, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The constellation of DNA repair functions in D. radiodurans is unremarkable by bacterial standards.
source: However, the constellation of DNA repair functions in D. radiodurans is unremarkable by bacterial standards.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about bacterial DNA repair systems.

claim: D. radiodurans and other IR resistant species appear to have approximately the same toolbox of DNA repair pathways as non-resistant species.
source: D. radiodurans and other IR resistant species appear to have approximately the same toolbox of DNA repair pathways as non-resistant species.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about bacterial DNA repair systems.

claim: The argument has been advanced that specialized DNA repair plays little or no role in IR resistance.
source: Thus, the argument has been advanced that specialized DNA repair plays little or no role in IR resistance (Daly, 2012, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Antioxidants prevent protein oxidation and render the classical DNA repair systems more readily available to correct the effects of IR.
source: Instead, antioxidants prevent protein oxidation and render the classical DNA repair systems more readily available to correct the effects of IR.
evidence: This claim is based on the hypothesis presented in cited literature.

claim: E. coli could acquire an extreme IR resistance phenotype by directed evolution.
source: In an earlier study, we demonstrated that the naturally IR sensitive bacterium, E. coli, could acquire an extreme IR resistance phenotype by directed evolution (Harris et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the authors' previous experimental work.

claim: 20 rounds of selection were carried out, with each round consisting of IR exposure sufficient to kill ∼99% of the population, followed by outgrowth.
source: In brief, we carried out 20 rounds of selection, with each round consisting of IR exposure sufficient to kill ∼99% of the population, followed by outgrowth.
evidence: This claim describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: The experiment was carried out four times, generating four separately evolved populations (IR-1-20, IR-2-20, IR-3-20, and IR-4-20).
source: The experiment was carried out four times, generating four separately evolved populations (IR-1-20, IR-2-20, IR-3-20, and IR-4-20).
evidence: This claim describes the experimental design.

claim: In the evolved populations, survival at 3000 Gy was typically increased by 3–4 orders of magnitude.
source: In the evolved populations, survival at 3000 Gy was typically increased by 3–4 orders of magnitude (Harris et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the cited previous study.

claim: Genetic alterations in the evolved strains were quite numerous (within the range of 40–80 per isolate).
source: Genetic alterations in the evolved strains were quite numerous (within the range of 40–80 per isolate), suggesting a complex and somewhat variable pattern of genetic innovation.
evidence: This claim is supported by genomic sequencing data from the previous study.

claim: None of the isolates in the earlier study had mutator phenotypes relative to the Founder strain.
source: None of the isolates in that study had mutator phenotypes relative to the Founder strain, although it is possible that mutators appear and thrive in the various populations for periods during the many cycles of selection (Harris et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the cited previous study.

claim: An approximately fivefold variation in levels of resistance to IR was evident in a screen of 62 separate isolates from population IR-1-20.
source: An approximately fivefold variation in levels of resistance to IR was evident in a screen of 62 separate isolates from population IR-1-20 (Harris et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the cited previous study.

claim: The complete genomic sequences of 13 new isolates from populations IR-2-20, IR-3-20, and IR-4-20 were obtained.
source: In the present study, we augmented the earlier data with the complete genomic sequences of 13 new isolates from populations IR-2-20, IR-3-20, and IR-4-20.
evidence: This claim describes the experimental work performed in the current study.

claim: The complete genomic sequences of nine isolates derived from either 20 or 30 rounds of further evolution of CB1000 were examined.
source: In addition, we examined the complete genomic sequences of nine isolates derived from either 20 or 30 rounds of further evolution of CB1000, an isolate derived from IR-1-20.
evidence: This claim describes the experimental work performed in the current study.

claim: IR resistance in the more highly evolved population (IR-CB1000-30) was impossible to measure accurately because the cells grew during irradiation at 6 Gy/min.
source: We note that IR resistance in this more highly evolved population (IR-CB1000-30) was impossible to measure accurately. The cells in this population grew more slowly than the Founder, but growth continued during irradiation at 6 Gy/min (John R Battista, unpublished data).
evidence: This claim is supported by unpublished experimental observations.

claim: In the isolates derived from the original four evolved populations, there were between 44 and 77 genetic alterations.
source: In the isolates derived from the original four evolved populations, there were between 44 and 77 genetic alterations.
evidence: This claim is supported by genomic sequencing data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The numbers of mutations jumped appreciably in the isolates derived from the further evolution of CB1000, with 242–267 mutations present in these strains.
source: The numbers of mutations jumped appreciably in the isolates derived from the further evolution of CB1000, with 242–267 mutations present in these strains.
evidence: This claim is supported by genomic sequencing data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Transition mutations dominated the mutational spectrum.
source: Transition mutations dominated the mutational spectrum.
evidence: This claim is supported by the mutational spectrum data presented in Table 1.

claim: The only genetic change that is universal to all strains sequenced is deletion of the e14 prophage.
source: One straightforward pattern noted in the earlier study was continued. The only genetic change that is universal to all strains sequenced is deletion of the e14 prophage, a defective lambdoid prophage that is 15.4 kb in length.
evidence: This claim is supported by genomic sequencing data from both the current and previous studies.

claim: The e14 prophage is a defective lambdoid prophage that is 15.4 kb in length.
source: The only genetic change that is universal to all strains sequenced is deletion of the e14 prophage, a defective lambdoid prophage that is 15.4 kb in length.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about the e14 prophage.

claim: The deletion of e14 occurs early, within the first three rounds of selection for IR resistance.
source: The deletion of occurs early, within the first three rounds of selection for IR resistance (EA Wood and JR Battista, unpublished data)
evidence: This claim is supported by unpublished experimental data.

claim: The e14 deletion makes a significant contribution (an approximately 10-fold increase in survival at 3000 Gy) to the overall IR resistance phenotype.
source: and it makes a significant contribution (an approximately 10-fold increase in survival at 3000 Gy) to the overall IR resistance phenotype (Harris et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the cited previous study.

claim: Population IR-1-20 has a particularly complex population structure and is strikingly different from the IR-2-20 and IR-3-20 populations.
source: Population IR-1-20 has a particularly complex population structure and is strikingly different from the IR-2-20 and IR-3-20 populations.
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of genomic sequencing data.

claim: Outside of the e14 deletion, there are no mutations shared by all seven of the IR-1-20 isolates.
source: Outside of the e14 deletion, there are no mutations shared by all seven of the IR-1-20 isolates.
evidence: This claim is supported by genomic sequencing data.

claim: There are three groupings of mutations in subsets of the clonal isolates that reflect clonal interference in the IR-1-20 population.
source: There are three groupings of mutations in subsets of the clonal isolates that reflect clonal interference (Gerrish and Lenski, 1998, Perron et al., 2012,Rozen et al., 2002) in this population (JR Battista, unpublished results).
evidence: This claim is supported by genomic sequencing data and unpublished analysis, with the concept of clonal interference supported by citations.

claim: Isolates from the IR-2-20 population exhibit 23 mutations that are present in all seven isolates from this population.
source: In contrast, isolates from the IR-2-20 and IR-3-20 populations each exhibit a number of mutations (23 in IR-2-20 and 30 in IR-3-20) that are present in all seven isolates from their respective populations, and are effectively fixed.
evidence: This claim is supported by genomic sequencing data.

claim: Isolates from the IR-3-20 population exhibit 30 mutations that are present in all seven isolates from this population.
source: In contrast, isolates from the IR-2-20 and IR-3-20 populations each exhibit a number of mutations (23 in IR-2-20 and 30 in IR-3-20) that are present in all seven isolates from their respective populations, and are effectively fixed.
evidence: This claim is supported by genomic sequencing data.

claim: CB2000 is one of the most radiation resistant of the isolated strains from the original evolved populations.
source: First, CB2000 is one of the most radiation resistant of the isolated strains from the original evolved populations (Harris et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the cited previous study.

claim: CB2000 was isolated from a population that lacks any sign of clonal interference.
source: Third, it was isolated from a population that lacks any sign of clonal interference, allowing us to focus on patterns present in a relatively simple population.
evidence: This claim is supported by genomic sequencing data analysis.

claim: Every evolved isolate sequenced features a mutation in one or another component of the replication restart primosome (priA, priC, dnaB, dnaT).
source: Every evolved isolate sequenced features a mutation in one or another component of the replication restart primosome (priA, priC, dnaB, dnaT), critical for the origin-independent restart of stalled DNA replication forks after recombinational DNA repair has occurred (Cox et al., 2000, Marians, 2008; Rangarajan and Woodgate RGoodman, 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by genomic sequencing data from all isolates.

claim: The replication restart primosome is critical for the origin-independent restart of stalled DNA replication forks after recombinational DNA repair has occurred.
source: Every evolved isolate sequenced features a mutation in one or another component of the replication restart primosome (priA, priC, dnaB, dnaT), critical for the origin-independent restart of stalled DNA replication forks after recombinational DNA repair has occurred (Cox et al., 2000, Marians, 2008; Rangarajan and Woodgate RGoodman, 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature and established knowledge.

claim: A mutation in the recA gene appears in 13 of 22 isolates from the original four evolved populations.
source: A mutation in the recA gene appears in 13 of 22 isolates from the original four evolved populations, appearing in every evolved population except IR-3-20.
evidence: This claim is supported by genomic sequencing data.

claim: The RecA D276N substitution is fixed in IR-2-20 (including CB2000).
source: The RecA D276N substitution is fixed in IR-2-20 (including CB2000), and the identical allele also appears in the separately evolved isolate from IR-4-20, CB4000.
evidence: This claim is supported by genomic sequencing data.

claim: The identical RecA D276N allele appears in the separately evolved isolate from IR-4-20, CB4000.
source: The RecA D276N substitution is fixed in IR-2-20 (including CB2000), and the identical allele also appears in the separately evolved isolate from IR-4-20, CB4000.
evidence: This claim is supported by genomic sequencing data.

claim: Two different variants of RecA, D276A and A289S, appear in strains derived from population IR-1-20.
source: Two different variants of RecA, D276A and A289S, appear in strains derived from population IR-1-20, helping to define two of the three sub-populations exhibiting clonal interference.
evidence: This claim is supported by genomic sequencing data.

claim: Mutations in the cryptic helicase gene yfjK are present in three of the four populations.
source: Mutations in the cryptic helicase gene yfjK are present in three of the four populations, although a mutation appears in only one of three sub-populations of IR-1-20.
evidence: This claim is supported by genomic sequencing data.

claim: The rsx gene cluster encodes a multi-subunit complex involved in the reduction of SoxR, part of a regulatory circuit for up to 50 target genes.
source: The rsx gene cluster encodes a multi-subunit complex involved in the reduction of SoxR, part of a regulatory circuit for up to 50 target genes.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about the rsx gene cluster.

claim: Some genes regulated by SoxR are directly involved in protection against reactive oxygen species.
source: Some of these are directly involved in protection against reactive oxygen species (Demple, 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The gsiB gene encodes an ABC transporter for glutathione.
source: The gsiB gene encodes an ABC transporter for glutathione.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about the gsiB gene.

claim: Different mutations in gsiB are fixed in IR-2-20 and IR-3-20.
source: Different mutations in gsiB are fixed in IR-2-20 and IR-3-20.
evidence: This claim is supported by genomic sequencing data.

claim: The products of the wca operon are involved in the synthesis of secreted exopolysaccharides that confer significant resistance to heat and acid stress.
source: The products of the wca operon are involved in the synthesis of secreted exopolysaccharides that confer significant resistance to heat and acid stress (Mao et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The nan operon is involved in the recycling and/or synthesis of components of the bacterial cell wall, particularly N-acetylmannosamine and N-acetylneuraminate.
source: The nan operon is involved in the recycling and/or synthesis of components of the bacterial cell wall, particularly N-acetylmannosamine and N-acetylneuraminate (Plumbridge and Vimr, 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Moving the CB2000 alleles of gsiB, rsxB, glpD, and wcaK individually into the Founder Δe14 background resulted in small increases in radioresistance, ranging from 2 (wcaK)–7 (gsiB) fold.
source: As illustrated in Figure 2A, moving the CB2000 alleles of gsiB, rsxB, glpD, and wcaK individually into the Founder Δe14 background resulted in small increases in radioresistance, ranging from 2 (wcaK)–7 (gsiB) fold.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Moving the CB2000 alleles encoding the RecA D276N, YfjK A151D, or DnaB P80H proteins individually into Founder Δe14 resulted in 1–2 log increases in IR resistance.
source: In contrast, moving the CB2000 alleles encoding the RecA D276N, YfjK A151D, or DnaB P80H proteins individually into Founder Δe14 resulted in 1–2 log increases in IR resistance, indicating that these mutations contribute in a more substantial way to the observed IR resistance of CB2000.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Of the three mutations (recA, dnaB, yfjK), the yfjK mutation had the greatest effect when present alone in the Founder Δe14 background.
source: Of these three mutations, the yfjK mutation had the greatest effect when present alone in the Founder Δe14 background (Figure 2A; the effects of these three mutations are summarized in Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and 2D.

claim: Individually reverting the recA, dnaB, and yfjK alleles back to the Founder sequence resulted in 1–2 log decreases in resistance.
source: The effects of the individual mutations on IR resistance in the Founder Δe14 background were echoed by the effects of reverting these same mutations to wild type in the CB2000 background (Figure 2B). Individually reverting the recA, dnaB, and yfjK alleles back to the Founder sequence resulted in 1–2 log decreases in resistance.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The recA reversion resulted in the largest loss of resistance with an approximately 50-fold decrease in IR resistance relative to CB2000.
source: In this case, the recA reversion resulted in the largest loss of resistance with an approximately 50-fold decrease in IR resistance relative to CB2000.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Reverting the other mutant alleles (gsiB, rsxB, glpD, wcaK, and nanE) to wild type in the CB2000 background had significant but relatively small effects.
source: Reverting the other mutant alleles (gsiB, rsxB, glpD, wcaK, and nanE) to wild type in the CB2000 background had significant but relatively small effects.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The deletion of the e14 prophage along with point mutations in recA, dnaB, and yfjK accounted for much of the radiation resistance of CB2000.
source: As shown in Figure 2A, the deletion of the e14 prophage along with point mutations in recA, dnaB, and yfjK accounted for much of the radiation resistance of CB2000.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: A strain incorporating the recA, dnaB, yfjK, wcaK, and gsiB mutations accounted for all but twofold of the overall increase in radiation resistance in CB2000.
source: A strain incorporating the recA, dnaB, yfjK, wcaK, and gsiB mutations accounted for all but twofold of the overall increase in radiation resistance in CB2000.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The radiation resistant phenotype observed in CB2000 was eliminated–in its entirety–by converting only the recA, dnaB, and yfjK genes back to the wild type sequence.
source: Figure 2B,D illustrate that the radiation resistant phenotype observed in CB2000 was eliminated–in its entirety–by converting only these three genes back to the wild type sequence.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and 2D.

claim: Mutations in recA and dnaB appear to affect the same pathway, as a combination of the recA and dnaB mutations in the Founder Δe14 background did not increase resistance beyond that observed for the dnaB mutation alone.
source: Mutations in recA and dnaB appear to affect the same pathway, as a combination of the recA and dnaB mutations in the Founder Δe14 background did not increase resistance beyond that observed for the dnaB mutation alone.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and inferred from the lack of additive effects.

claim: Combining the yfjK mutation with those in dnaB and recA generates a further increase in IR resistance, suggesting that the yfjK mutation affects a different cellular process or pathway than the other two.
source: Combining the yfjK mutation with those in dnaB and recA generates a further increase in IR resistance (Figure 2A,D), suggesting that the yfjK mutation affects a different cellular process or pathway than the other two.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and 2D, with the interpretation based on inference.

claim: When CB2000 (Ara−) was mixed in a 1:1 ratio with CB2000 in which the recA, dnaB, and yfjK mutations had been converted to wild type, and irradiated at 2000 and 3000 Gy, CB2000 exhibited at least a 2 log advantage in survival at the higher IR dose.
source: When CB2000 (Ara−) was mixed in a 1:1 ratio with CB2000 in which the recA, dnaB, and yfjK mutations had been converted to wild type, and irradiated at 2000 and 3000 Gy, CB2000 exhibited at least a 2 log advantage in survival at the higher IR dose (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by competition experiment data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Founder Δe14 (Ara−) mixed with an isogenic strain carrying the recA, dnaB, and yfjK mutations showed a 2 log advantage for the strain incorporating the three mutations after irradiation at 2000 Gy.
source: Similarly, Founder Δe14 (Ara−) was mixed with an isogenic strain carrying the recA, dnaB, and yfjK mutations. A 2 log advantage for the strain incorporating the three mutations was seen after irradiation at 2000 Gy (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by competition experiment data shown in Figure 3B and 3C.

claim: When CB2000 in which the recA, dnaB, and yfjK mutations had been converted to wild type was mixed with Founder Δe14 (Ara−), survival of the two strains was similar (the CB2000 reversion strain had less than a 0.5 log advantage).
source: When CB2000 in which the recA, dnaB, and yfjK mutations had been converted to wild type was mixed with Founder Δe14 (Ara−), survival of the two strains was similar (the CB2000 reversion strain had less than a 0.5 log advantage [Figure 3D,E]).
evidence: This claim is supported by competition experiment data shown in Figure 3D and 3E.

claim: Strains deleted for wcaK, gsiB, glpD, and nanE respectively are twofold to threefold more resistant than Founder Δe14.
source: Strains deleted for wcaK, gsiB, glpD, and nanE respectively are twofold to threefold more resistant than Founder Δe14.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: For wcaK and glpD, the increase in resistance from deletion is similar to the resistance observed in Founder Δe14 strains carrying the point mutations in these genes, suggesting that the mutations result in loss of function.
source: For wcaK and glpD, this increase in resistance is similar to the resistance observed in Founder Δe14 strains carrying the point mutations in these genes, suggesting that the mutations result in loss of function.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C and inference from the comparison.

claim: Founder Δe14 ΔyfjK cells are 13-fold more resistant than the isogenic parent strain.
source: Founder Δe14 ΔyfjK cells are 13-fold more resistant than the isogenic parent strain as illustrated in Figure 2C.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The Founder Δe14 strain encoding YfjK A151D is an additional 10-fold more resistant than the yfjK deletion, and nearly 2 orders of magnitude more resistant than Founder Δe14.
source: However, the Founder Δe14 strain encoding YfjK A151D is an additional 10-fold more resistant than the deletion, and nearly 2 orders of magnitude more resistant than Founder Δe14.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: It is possible that the mutation in yfjK is a partial loss of function, or that it eliminates one or more activities of the YfjK protein but not all of them.
source: It is possible that the mutation in yfjK is a partial loss of function, or that it eliminates one or more activities of the YfjK protein but not all of them.
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on the observation that the point mutation has a different effect than the deletion.

claim: Mutations affecting the clpXP complex are prominent in populations IR-1-20 and IR-3-20.
source: Mutations affecting the clpXP complex are prominent in populations IR-1-20 and IR-3-20, and new mutations potentially affecting this system also appear in the further evolution of CB1000.
evidence: This claim is supported by genomic sequencing data shown in Table 2.

claim: clpXP encodes a proteolytic system involved in turnover of many key cellular proteins including many involved in DNA metabolism.
source: clpXP encodes a proteolytic system involved in turnover of many key cellular proteins including many involved in DNA metabolism (Baker and Sauer, 2006)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature and established knowledge.

claim: clpXP is essential for the transition from growth to stationary phase.
source: and is essential for the transition from growth to stationary phase.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about the clpXP system.

claim: A mutation in fnr is fixed in IR-3-20.
source: A mutation in fnr is fixed in IR-3-20.
evidence: This claim is supported by genomic sequencing data shown in Table 2.

claim: A mutation that leads to a truncated Fnr protein appears in all nine isolates derived from the further evolution of CB1000.
source: While this gene is not targeted in any of the other three original populations, its importance is suggested by the appearance of a mutation that leads to a truncated Fnr protein in all nine isolates derived from the further evolution of CB1000 (Supplementary file 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by genomic sequencing data.

claim: Fnr is a regulator that oversees the transition between aerobic and anaerobic metabolism.
source: Fnr is a regulator that oversees the transition between aerobic and anaerobic metabolism (Kiley and Beinert, 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature and established knowledge.

claim: There were few genes with different expression profiles when comparing the Founder, CB1000, and CB2000 strains with a 1.5-fold cutoff enforced.
source: Overall, there were few genes with different expression profiles when comparing the strains with a 1.5-fold cutoff enforced.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq data analysis.

claim: The only commonality in expression patterns between the evolved strains was the >1.5-fold decrease in the transcript abundance compared to Founder of the following genes: fruBKA (fructose metabolism), sdaC (serine transport) and proK (proline tRNA).
source: The only commonality in expression patterns between the evolved strains was the >1.5-fold decrease in the transcript abundance compared to Founder of the following genes: fruBKA (fructose metabolism), sdaC (serine transport) and proK (proline tRNA).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq data analysis.

claim: There are no significant changes in metabolites between any of the strains measured, with the possible exception of small apparent decreases in the levels of acetate and succinate in CB2000 as compared to Founder.
source: There are no significant changes in metabolites between any of the strains measured, with the possible exception of small apparent decreases in the levels of acetate and succinate in CB2000 as compared to Founder.
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR metabolite analysis data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Unlike D. radiodurans, there is no evidence of accumulation of intermediate metabolites that could act as antioxidants in the evolved E. coli strains.
source: Unlike D. radiodurans, there is no evidence of accumulation of intermediate metabolites that could act as antioxidants.
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR metabolite analysis data and comparison to D. radiodurans.

claim: In spite of the demonstrable increases in radiation resistance exhibited by all of the isolates, there was not a significant change in the Mn/Fe ratio in most of the directly evolved highly radioresistant strains of E. coli.
source: In spite of the demonstrable increases in radiation resistance exhibited by all of our isolates, we did not see a significant change in the Mn/Fe ratio (nor significant increases in the concentration of either metal) in most of our directly evolved highly radioresistant strains of E. coli.
evidence: This claim is supported by trace metal analysis data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: There is a minor elevation in manganese in the one evolved isolate from population IR-4-20 (CB4000) and in some strains derived from the further evolution of CB1000.
source: There is a minor elevation in manganese in the one evolved isolate from population IR-4-20 (CB4000) and in some strains derived from the further evolution of CB1000.
evidence: This claim is supported by trace metal analysis data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: There is no universal change in metal content in the evolved strains that mirror the apparent adaptation seen in D. radiodurans and other IR-resistant bacteria.
source: There is no universal change in metal content in the evolved strains that mirror the apparent adaptation seen in D. radiodurans and other IR-resistant bacteria.
evidence: This claim is supported by trace metal analysis data and comparison to D. radiodurans.

claim: IR resistance can be increased—dramatically—by functional enhancement and/or adaptation of existing DNA repair enzymes.
source: IR resistance can be increased—dramatically—by functional enhancement and/or adaptation of existing DNA repair enzymes.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental findings that mutations in DNA repair genes account for most of the IR resistance.

claim: Classical DNA repair pathways can adapt to facilitate more efficient repair when cells are exposed to high levels of IR.
source: Classical DNA repair pathways can adapt to facilitate more efficient repair when cells are exposed to high levels of IR.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental findings and represents an inference from the data.

claim: In one well-characterized isolate, three mutations—all in DNA repair functions—largely account for the increase in IR resistance.
source: In one well-characterized isolate, three mutations—all in DNA repair functions—largely account for the increase in IR resistance.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that three mutations in recA, dnaB, and yfjK account for most of the IR resistance in CB2000.

claim: The metabolic profile of the evolved cells indicates that they possess little or no unusual gene expression, metabolite concentration, or metal ion adaptations when they first encounter irradiation.
source: The metabolic profile of our cells indicates that the evolved strains possess little or no unusual gene expression, metabolite concentration, or metal ion adaptations when they first encounter irradiation.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq, NMR metabolite analysis, and trace metal analysis data.

claim: In CB2000, changes in the rsxB gene might bring about some significant and beneficial changes in the IR response.
source: In CB2000, changes in the rsxB gene might bring about some significant and beneficial changes in the IR response.
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on the presence of mutations in rsxB and its known function.

claim: In the case of CB2000, it is clear that changes to DNA repair genes—not regulatory genes—play the major role in the observed IR resistance.
source: However, in the case of CB2000, it is clear that changes to DNA repair genes—not regulatory genes—play the major role in the observed IR resistance.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that mutations in DNA repair genes account for most of the IR resistance.

claim: The complement of DNA repair systems present tend to be quite similar from one bacterial species to another, but they are not identical.
source: The complement of DNA repair systems present tend to be quite similar from one bacterial species to another, but they are not identical.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about bacterial DNA repair systems.

claim: Whereas Deinococcus radiodurans has a fairly standard set of DNA repair functions, there are important distinctions in both the relevant gene catalogue and the mechanisms used to recover from exposure to high levels of ionizing radiation.
source: Whereas Deinococcus radiodurans has a fairly standard set of DNA repair functions (Daly, MJ, 2012), there are important distinctions in both the relevant gene catalogue (Cox and Battista, 2005, Blasius et al., 2008) and the mechanisms used to recover from exposure to high levels of ionizing radiation (Slade et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Evolution of a complex extremophile phenotype, such as extreme resistance to ionizing radiation, has no single molecular explanation.
source: Evolution of a complex extremophile phenotype, such as extreme resistance to ionizing radiation, has no single molecular explanation.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the observation of multiple contributing mutations and mechanisms.

claim: There are multiple paths; multiple mutations affecting multiple cellular systems make significant contributions to IR resistance.
source: There are multiple paths; multiple mutations affecting multiple cellular systems make significant contributions.
evidence: This claim is supported by the genomic sequencing data showing diverse mutations across different populations.

claim: The mutational patterns suggest that improvements in the amelioration of protein oxidation may also play a role in some of the evolved populations.
source: The mutational patterns suggest that improvements in the amelioration of protein oxidation, as first pointed out by Daly et al. (Daly et al., 2004, Slade and Radman, 2011, Krisko and Radman, 2010, Daly, 2012, 2009), may also play a role in some of the evolved populations.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the presence of mutations in genes related to oxidative stress response.

claim: Although the role of protein oxidation amelioration appears to be relatively minor in CB2000, it may well predominate in one or more of the other populations.
source: Although that role appears to be relatively minor in CB2000, it may well predominate in one or more of the other populations.
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on the observation of different mutational patterns in different populations.

claim: Any mechanisms contributing to the amelioration of protein oxidation in these isolates may be somewhat different than those described to date for D. radiodurans.
source: Given the genes affected, any mechanisms contributing to the amelioration of protein oxidation in these isolates may be somewhat different than those described to date for D. radiodurans.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the different genes affected in the evolved E. coli strains compared to D. radiodurans.

claim: The altered RecA proteins nucleate filament formation more rapidly and extend those filaments more slowly than the wild-type protein, leading to larger numbers of shorter filaments.
source: In brief, the altered RecA proteins nucleate filament formation more rapidly and extend those filaments more slowly than the wild-type protein, leading to larger numbers of shorter filaments.

claim: The altered RecA proteins function better as shorter filaments, and are less sensitive to inhibition by ADP.

claim: The altered RecA proteins exhibit functional alterations that are easily rationalized in the context of a recombinational system that must simultaneously deal with large numbers of double strand breaks in cells where metabolic processes might be compromised.
source: In general, the proteins exhibit functional alterations that are easily rationalized in the context of a recombinational system that must simultaneously deal with large numbers of double strand breaks in cells where metabolic processes might be compromised.
